entries.title: Isolation Forest Anomaly Detector
entries.why: Isolation Forest is ideal for multivariate anomaly detection in sensor data. It works by 'isolating' anomalies - unusual data points require fewer random splits to separate from normal data, giving them lower scores.
entries.whatItDoes: Imports scikit-learn's IsolationForest (the core ML algorithm), StandardScaler (feature normalization), joblib (model persistence), pandas (data manipulation), and psycopg2 (database access for training data).

entries.title: All 50 Sensor Feature Columns
entries.why: The detector needs to know which columns to use for training and inference. These 50 parameters span 5 categories: Environmental (10), Mechanical (10), Thermal (10), Electrical (10), and Fluid Dynamics (10).
entries.whatItDoes: Defines the AnomalyDetector class and its SENSOR_COLUMNS list - all 50 sensor parameters that the ML model uses as features. The order must match the database schema for consistent feature vectors.
entries.perfNotes: 50 features is manageable for Isolation Forest (no curse of dimensionality like KNN)

entries.title: Detector Initialization & Model Loading
entries.why: The detector should persist trained models to avoid retraining on every startup. Initialization checks for existing models and loads them if available, enabling fast cold starts.
entries.whatItDoes: 1) Sets contamination rate (expected anomaly proportion) and n_estimators from config, 2) Creates IsolationForest with random_state=42 for reproducibility, 3) Initializes StandardScaler for feature normalization, 4) Checks models directory and loads existing model if present.

failureModes.recovery: Model will be retrained on next detect() call

entries.perfNotes: n_jobs=-1 uses all CPU cores for training/inference

entries.title: Model Persistence with joblib
entries.why: Trained models should be saved to disk so they survive restarts. joblib is preferred over pickle for scikit-learn models because it handles numpy arrays more efficiently.
entries.whatItDoes: Saves a dictionary containing: the trained IsolationForest model, the fitted StandardScaler, and feature statistics (means/stds) used for contribution analysis.

failureModes.recovery: Model works in-memory but lost on restart

entries.securityNotes: Model files should be protected - malicious models could produce bad predictions

entries.title: Training Data Fetch from TimescaleDB
entries.why: Isolation Forest learns 'normal' patterns from historical data. It needs enough examples of normal operation to establish a baseline. Data is fetched from the sensor_readings table.
entries.whatItDoes: 1) Connects to PostgreSQL, 2) Queries last N readings (ORDER BY created_at DESC), 3) Returns pandas DataFrame with all 50 sensor columns plus reading ID.

failureModes.recovery: Training will fail, detection returns False
Training fails due to insufficient data

entries.perfNotes: LIMIT clause prevents memory issues with large tables

entries.title: Model Training Pipeline
entries.why: Training fits the Isolation Forest to 'normal' data. After training, the model can score new readings - lower scores (more negative) indicate more anomalous data.
entries.whatItDoes: 1) Fetches training data if not provided, 2) Validates MIN_TRAINING_SAMPLES, 3) Fills NaN values with column means, 4) Stores feature means/stds for contribution analysis, 5) Scales data with StandardScaler, 6) Fits IsolationForest, 7) Saves model to disk.

failureModes.recovery: Wait for more data to accumulate
Check data quality, fix upstream issues

tests.how: Generate 500 normal readings, verify is_trained becomes True

entries.perfNotes: Training 1000 samples with 100 trees takes ~1-2 seconds

entries.title: Identify Contributing Sensors via Z-Score
entries.why: When an anomaly is detected, operators need to know WHICH sensors are unusual. Z-score analysis identifies sensors that deviate significantly from their historical means.
entries.whatItDoes: For each sensor, calculates z-score: (value - mean) / std. Sensors with |z-score| > threshold_std (default 2.0) are considered contributors. Returns list of sensor names.

entries.title: Real-Time Anomaly Detection
entries.why: This is the HOT PATH - called for every incoming sensor reading. It must be fast (< 10ms) to handle real-time data streams without backpressure.
entries.whatItDoes: 1) Auto-trains if not trained, 2) Converts reading dict to feature array, 3) Wraps in DataFrame (sklearn compat), 4) Scales features, 5) Calls model.predict() (-1=anomaly, 1=normal), 6) Gets decision_function score (lower=more anomalous), 7) Identifies contributing sensors if anomaly.

failureModes.condition: Model not trained and training fails
failureModes.recovery: No detection until model can be trained

entries.title: Database Recording & Singleton Pattern
entries.why: Anomaly detections should be persisted for historical analysis, reporting, and ML retraining. The singleton pattern ensures one detector instance is reused across the application.
entries.whatItDoes: record_anomaly_detection() inserts into anomaly_detections table with: reading_id, method ('isolation_forest'), score, is_anomaly flag, and contributing sensors array. get_detector() returns a global singleton instance.

failureModes.recovery: Anomaly is detected but not recorded

entries.perfNotes: INSERT is async-safe with RETURNING for immediate ID access
